notes: THE FORGE -- three pieces of one slot and one rank, and gold, make one of the rank above (client/scenes/pages/forge_page.gd, layout client/layout/forge.json).

This painting sat unused in ~/Downloads/Emperors_Design_Pack while the forge was a Dialog.ask with its numbers written out in a sentence. The pack's own brief for it reads: 'three EMPTY square sockets in a row ... a glowing gold arrow pointing down to a larger, radiant EMPTY result socket ... a small gold coin beside an EMPTY cost plate, and an EMPTY odds plate beside a small round gold i button.' That is exactly what the page fills.

MEASURED off the painting's own gold. The three sockets stand at x 124, 372 and 620 (pitch 248), y 737, each 197x192. The result socket is 224x214 at (359,1040). The cost plate is (208,1281,239,68), the odds plate (515,1281,229,68), the coin (126,1277,84,72) and the i button (758,1280,69,67). FORGE is (71,1387,456,121) and CLOSE (540,1387,331,121).

Nothing is erased: every socket and every plate is painted EMPTY, so what the page draws goes straight over the painting's own ground. A piece in a socket is the Armory's own object -- the tier's velvet, its rarity ring and the piece's painting (ItemGround.in_ringed_tile) -- laid inside the painted gold, so one piece of gear looks the same in the bag and on the anvil.
